requirements.definition: The X argument of IEEE_SUPPORT_SUBNORMAL shall be of type real.

requirements.title: IEEE_SUPPORT_SUBNORMAL reports datatype plus subnormal arithmetic and assignment support for X kind
requirements.definition: IEEE_SUPPORT_SUBNORMAL(X) is true exactly for real kind type parameters for which IEEE_SUPPORT_DATATYPE(X) is true and the processor supports arithmetic operations and assignments with subnormal numbers, and false otherwise.

pending.ieee-support-subnormal-kind-inquiry: Probe IEEE_SUPPORT_SUBNORMAL(x) for default and selected nondefault real variables; true branch performs datatype, arithmetic, and assignment facets, false branch records an unsupported skip, and mutation inverts the recorded logical result.
pending.ieee-support-subnormal-true-implies-data: Evaluate IEEE_SUPPORT_SUBNORMAL(x) and IEEE_SUPPORT_DATATYPE(x); true branch for subnormal support asserts datatype support is also true, and mutation expects datatype false.
pending.ieee-support-subnormal-true-branch-arith: Probe IEEE_SUPPORT_SUBNORMAL(x), IEEE_SUPPORT_DATATYPE(x), RADIX(x)==2, and DIGITS(x)>=4; true branch chooses even q by parity: MINEXPONENT(x)-3 on even parity, otherwise MINEXPONENT(x)-4, hand-checks MINEXPONENT-DIGITS <= q <= MINEXPONENT-3, constructs sub=SCALE(1.0_kind,q), assigns it through a sentinel variable, asserts 0.0 < sub and sub < TINY(x), and asserts exact sub+sub == SCALE(1.0_kind,q+1) with q+1 still below MINEXPONENT-1. False branches record unsupported skip. Mutation replaces sub with TINY(x).

requirements.title: IEEE_SUPPORT_SUBNORMAL without X reports all-real subnormal support
requirements.definition: IEEE_SUPPORT_SUBNORMAL() is true exactly when IEEE_SUPPORT_SUBNORMAL(X) is true for all real X, and false otherwise.

pending.ieee-support-subnormal-no-x-all-real-rel: Generate scalar representatives for every available real kind from ISO_FORTRAN_ENV REAL_KINDS, statically instantiating each kind as REAL(0.0,kind); assert IEEE_SUPPORT_SUBNORMAL() .EQV. ALL of the instantiated IEEE_SUPPORT_SUBNORMAL(REAL(0.0,kind)) results. This checks both directions: no-X true entails every X-form true, and all X-forms true entails no-X true. Mutation drops one kind-specific conjunct.
